tables.title: Figure 3: Comparison of swear word usage
tables.population: Year-wise Average Percent Swear Words in Songs (1970–2010)
notes: Figure 3 is a scatter plot titled 'Year-wise Average Percent Swear Words in Songs' with x-axis YEAR (1970–2010) and y-axis Percent (0–2.5).
Two series: blue circles for BB (Billboard), orange squares for MSD (Million Song Dataset).
Trend lines shown: dashed blue for BB, dotted orange for MSD.

The text states: 'From 1965 to 1995, popular songs used fewer swear words as compared to the other songs. However, from the 1990s there is a persistent trend of increasing swear word usage in popular songs.'
Exact numeric values are not printed on the plot; the above row values are approximate readings from the graph (e.g., at 2010, BB ≈ 2.0%, MSD ≈ 1.8%).
The y-axis max is 2.5, and data points do not exceed 2.0.

observations: Figure 1 shows word clouds for top 100 words in 1965 and 2015; 'love' was most popular in 1965, but not in 2015; 'rock' is more frequent than 'blues' in later years per Figure 2.
Figure 2 (Word Rank Plot) shows 'rock' rising in rank (i.e., becoming more popular/higher frequency) from ~1960 onward, while 'blues' remains relatively stable/declining.
Figure 3 shows swear word usage (%) increasing over time for both BB and MSD, with BB consistently higher than MSD.
The text mentions Figures 4a, 4b, 4c, and 5, but only Figures 1, 2, and 3 are visible on this page.
uncertainties: Figure 2 is labeled 'Figure 2: Year-wise rank comparison', but the text refers to 'Figure 2a' — possible labeling inconsistency.
No exact numerical data tables are provided for any figure; all values are inferred from visual plots, introducing reading error.
The word clouds in Figure 1 contain many overlapping words; exact ordering/ranking beyond top few (e.g., 'love' in 1965) is not quantitatively specified.
In Figure 3, the scatter points are not labeled with exact values; approximations used may deviate from true data.
The text states 'We measured the speed of a song as (length in words/duration in seconds)' but no table of speeds is shown on this page.
